boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Lewis's Farm record (March 29, 1865) in the Appomattox Campaign [March-April 1865]. White Oak Road (VA087) and Dinwiddie Court House (VA086) follow on March 31. The army-wide spring 1865 returns are cited here once, as campaign context. Army-wide returns, campaign-wide loss and prisoner totals, the April 9 paroles and the retreat as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Corps' and the live field zero. Humphreys says Chamberlain's brigade of Griffin's division met Wise's and Wallace's brigades of Anderson's command, with part of Bartlett's brigade joining toward the close, and that Lee had sent Anderson with Bushrod Johnson's division and Wise's brigade; Johnson says he advanced Wise's brigade with Wallace's, Moody's and Ransom's following. As campaign context, Humphreys gives the spring 1865 effective force from the latest returns as 69,000 infantry of the Army of the Potomac, 124,700 of all arms in the three Union commands, and not less than 46,000 infantry and 57,000 of all arms for Lee; his Appendix L gives the Army of the Potomac 3,064 officers and 68,956 enlisted infantry present for duty equipped on March 31 and Lee not less than 55,500 on the February 20 return, 'and probably on the 25th of March'.
claims.rationale: The engagement figures are formation lists only. The army-wide figures are Union effective and present-for-duty returns of March 31 and a Confederate return of February 20 (the last found), with Humphreys' own additions; his 57,000 and 55,500 for Lee differ in basis and are not reconciled. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.rationale: Direction attributed as stated; Anderson, not a frozen commander, directed the Confederate commitment and withdrawal in Johnson's account. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 750 (US 380; CS 370) and the live field 752 (US 381; CS 371). Humphreys gives Griffin's loss as 367 killed and wounded, some 200 Confederate prisoners and a Confederate loss 'evidently greater'; Johnson gives his loss as about 250, mainly from Wise's and Wallace's brigades, and the unsigned note printed after his report gives an aggregate of 183 for the Quaker road under a unit name garbled in OCR ('Muse').
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The note's unit and population are unclear and it is not added to Johnson's 250.

open_questions: Warren's, Griffin's, Chamberlain's and Bartlett's reports (Nos. 74, 75, 77, 78, 83), Wallace's report (No. 274), Anderson's and Wise's accounts, Lee's March 29 dispatches (selected for other records), the Union casualty return (No. 2) and the Confederate returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the commander of the Second Corps in this campaign, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; where it narrates his own corps it is a participant's account. It relies on the reports of Sheridan, Warren, Wright, Gibbon, Ewell and Fitzhugh Lee, on Confederate testimony before the Warren Court of Inquiry and on the returns, so it is not independent of those families. Lee's, Sheridan's, Bushrod Johnson's, Miles's, Gibbon's, Ewell's and Fitzhugh Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLVI, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
